children: Belgium's Rossel, which publishes local newspapers in French-speaking Belgium and northern France, such as Le Soir and La Voix du Nord, is set to buy French rival Sud Ouest, the two companies said on Thursday.

Groupe Sud Ouest, which owns regional newspapers in southern France beside the eponymous title such as Charente Libre, said a merger would produce a new entity with combined sales of more than 400 million euros ($464.8 million).
The Lemoine family which controls Sud Ouest has agreed to sell the media group, Rossel's Chief Executive Bernard Marchant was quoted as saying by Le Soir, the Belgian group's flagship newspaper.
He said he would not disclose the amount, Le Soir said, adding the transaction should be finalized by the end of this year.
The company did not respond to a request for comment.
Rossel, which is owned by the Belgian Hurbain family, took over its Belgian rival IPM, which runs newspapers such as La DH and La Libre, after local antitrust regulator authorized the deal in July.
